conditions.text: Set up: app version 3.2.0, Android 15, Pixel 8 — each held in all 3 events (support 1.0).

Also present in every event: push notifications were not deliverable (push.deliverable false) even though the OS permission was ALLOWED and provider registration was REGISTERED, and the profile was consistent; the packet does not state whether any of these matter for triggering the crash.

No condition in this packet is recorded as varying between events, so there is nothing identified here as optional — but the sample is only 3 events, so conditions that look required may simply be untested elsewhere.
Memory state, feed size and page count are not captured in the packet and therefore cannot be listed as required or optional.

missing_evidence_questions.text: Can breadcrumbs be enabled or recovered for this crash, so the user actions immediately before the failure in loadPage are known?
How many feed pages had been loaded, and what was the heap usage, at the point of the 8388608-byte allocation?
What exactly does commit c32a444 change in src/modules/news/feed.ts around line 88, and did the crash start only in builds containing it?
Does the crash occur on devices or OS versions other than Pixel 8 / Android 15, and on versions other than 3.2.0, or is the observed uniformity just an artifact of having only 3 events?
Is the push.deliverable=false state with ALLOWED permission and REGISTERED provider related to this crash at all, or incidental to these 3 events?

steps_prose.text: Install app version 3.2.0 on a Pixel 8 running Android 15 — that is the exact configuration present in all 3 events.
Drive the news feed paging path so that src/modules/news/feed.ts:88 executes loadPage, since that is the culprit frame recorded for the crash.
Keep paging until an 8388608-byte (8 MB) allocation is attempted and fails with OutOfMemoryError.
The number of pages, the feed content and any other user actions needed are not known: breadcrumbs are missing for all 3 events, so no action sequence can be reconstructed from this packet.

As a lead rather than a proven cause, commit c32a444 ("MEI-52: Local news feed paging") touches the same file, src/modules/news/feed.ts, so exercising the paging behaviour introduced or changed there is the most direct route to the failing frame.

summary.text: The incident is an OutOfMemoryError ("Failed to allocate 8388608 bytes") that surfaces in loadPage at src/modules/news/feed.ts:88, seen across the 3 events considered; the packet contains no breadcrumbs, so the exact moment and user action that triggers it are not recorded.
